query: Alphabet fiscal year 2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending
normalized: 2025 ai alphabet capital center data expenditure fiscal q3 spending year

output.content:
Alphabet’s **Q3 2025 capital expenditures were $24.0 billion**, with the vast majority directed to technical infrastructure supporting AI and cloud demand. [[1]] 

Alphabet allocated approximately **60%** of Q3 CapEx—about **$14.4 billion**—to servers, which includes AI compute infrastructure such as GPUs and Google’s TPUs. [[1]] 

Approximately **40%**—about **$9.6 billion**—went to data-center facilities and networking equipment. [[1]] 

Management said the buildout was driven by strong Cloud-customer demand and broader growth opportunities, while highlighting investments in NVIDIA GPUs and internally designed TPUs to expand AI infrastructure capacity. [[1]] 

At the time of the Q3 release on October 29, 2025, Alphabet raised its expected **full-year 2025 CapEx to $91 billion–$93 billion**, from its prior $85 billion outlook. [[1]] 

The higher infrastructure investment was already increasing earnings pressure: Q3 depreciation rose **$1.6 billion year over year to $5.6 billion**, or **41%**, and Alphabet expected depreciation growth to accelerate slightly in Q4, alongside higher data-center operating costs such as energy. [[1]] 

For context, Alphabet ultimately spent **$91.4 billion** in CapEx for full-year 2025; its later FY2026 plan called for **$175 billion–$185 billion**, illustrating the planned step-up in AI data-center investment. [[2]]
